references.text: The Israelites did not drive out the Canaanites living in Gezer, but allowed them to live among them as forced laborers - the same pattern seen in Judges 1:28.
When Israel became strong, they put the Canaanites to forced labor but did not completely drive them out - an almost identical situation.
The Benjaminites did not drive out the Jebusites living in Jerusalem - part of the same pattern of incomplete conquest.
Ephraim did not drive out the Canaanites in Gezer - the same theme of Israel's failure to obey by driving out the peoples.
Zebulun did not drive out the inhabitants of Kitron and Nahalol, but put them to forced labor - a parallel example.
Naphtali did not drive out the inhabitants, but put them to forced labor - the same pattern is repeated.
Solomon put the remaining peoples to forced labor - a continuation of the practice from the time of Judges.
God's warning that those who are not driven out will become a snare - the background for why Israel was to drive out the Canaanites.
